verdict.rationale: Open WebUI's own docs describe personal API keys that let external code call the same endpoints the web UI uses. The Computer gateway also exposes workspaces as an OpenAI-compatible model that any OpenAI-style client can drive, so programmatic control is a first-party capability. However, no published endpoint reference or OpenAPI spec is evidenced (all probed OpenAPI paths on the docs site returned 404), so how thoroughly the public API is documented is unproven. Missing for 10: a published API reference or OpenAPI/Swagger spec, documented coverage of endpoints beyond chat completions (e.g., managing chats, files, models, users), and independent or hands-on corroboration of driving the product via the API.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can drive the product through a documented public API

citations.quote: An API key is a personal access token that lets external code call the same endpoints the web UI uses.
The gateway exposes each of your workspaces as an OpenAI-compatible model, so any OpenAI-style client can run agent tasks in a real workspace.
